title: Minimum Bouquet Days
description:
# Minimum Bouquet Days

You are given an integer array `bloomDay`. The value `bloomDay[i]` is the day when the `i`-th flower blooms.

You must make exactly `m` bouquets. Each bouquet must use `k` **adjacent** flowers, and every flower in that bouquet must have bloomed on or before the chosen day. A flower can be used in at most one bouquet.

Return the earliest day when it is possible to make `m` bouquets. If there are not enough flowers to ever make the bouquets, return `-1`.

## Example 1:

**Input:** bloomDay = [1,10,3,10,2], m = 3, k = 1
**Output:** 3
**Explanation:** Each bouquet needs one flower. By day 3, three flowers have bloomed.

## Example 2:

**Input:** bloomDay = [1,10,3,10,2], m = 3, k = 2
**Output:** -1
**Explanation:** Making three bouquets of size two would require six flowers, but there are only five flowers.

## Constraints:

* `1 <= bloomDay.length <= 100000`
* `1 <= bloomDay[i] <= 1000000000`
* `1 <= m, k <= 1000000`

solutions.name: Binary Search Day
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use binary search over the answer day. For a fixed day, scan the garden left to right, count consecutive bloomed flowers, and greedily cut a bouquet whenever the run reaches `k`.

## Key Insight

Feasibility is monotonic: if day `d` can make enough bouquets, every later day can also make them. That turns the minimum-day question into a binary search on a yes/no predicate.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log M), where M is the maximum bloom day
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Binary Search Unique Bloom Days
solutions.description:
## Approach

Sort a copy of the bloom days and binary search over those candidate values instead of every integer day. Each candidate is checked with the same greedy consecutive-run predicate.

## Key Insight

The answer must be one of the actual bloom days. Searching sorted candidates keeps the monotonic structure while avoiding the full numeric range up to 1000000000.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Union Find Bloom Segments
solutions.description:
## Approach

Activate flowers in increasing bloom-day order. Union an activated position with active neighbors, track each connected segment size, and maintain how many bouquets all active segments can produce.

## Key Insight

For any fixed day, only contiguous active segments matter, and a segment of length `len` contributes `len / k` bouquets. Updating that contribution when segments merge avoids rescanning the whole garden for each day.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: TreeMap Active Intervals
solutions.description:
## Approach

Activate flowers by increasing bloom day and store active contiguous intervals in a `TreeMap` from start to end. When a new flower opens, merge with the left and right neighboring intervals if they touch, updating the total bouquet contribution.

## Key Insight

This is the same segment-contribution idea as union find, but keeping explicit interval boundaries makes it clear why adjacent bloomed flowers form non-overlapping bouquet capacity.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)
